paragraphs.source_en: Don Rodrigo, the former governor of Luzon, had paid his respects to Shogun Tokugawa Hidetada in Edo. paragraphs.source_en: Ōkubo Nagayasu had intended to inspect the mine at Doi-yama in Sagami, but came to Sunpu on the pretext that he had received orders from Ieyasu; Date Masamune likewise came on the pretext of reporting progress on the construction of Zuiganji at Matsushima. paragraphs.source_en: Two days after the audience, Ieyasu sent word through Honda Masazumi that he granted Rodrigo's three requests. At the same time, he said that if skilled miners could be found in Mexico, he wanted Rodrigo to send one hundred and fifty of them to Japan, or at least fifty.
